text:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: ALERT 1775022222 - edge-proxy AUTH 401 spike (x18/min) from 3 IPs. sample log lines show 'authorization' header fragments in debug logs -> possible token leakage to logshipper. Auto-escalate to #incidents.

alex (oncall-sre): saw it. I'm taking lead. Oncall window til 09:00PT. Marking P1 if we see customer requests failing. Starting basic mitigation checklist.

alex (oncall-sre): can someone from security join? I'm going to throttle the suspicious IPs at the WAF and pause the staging log-forwarder to external bucket.

maya (security): on it. I'm pulling recent logshipper configs. Suspect pipeline: staging-archiver-to-s3 (last deploy 03:12). If tokens are in logs that were forwarded, we need to contain and rotate any exposed creds.

jorge (eng-runtime): repro of the 401 pattern: client-id header present, but backend returns 401 and debug logger prints header snippet in the same stacktrace. That debug flag got toggled in a canary yesterday.

alex (oncall-sre): rolling back the debug flag on edge-proxy now: 
```
kubectl -n edge set env deploy/edge-proxy DEBUG=false
```
applied.

infra-bot: rollback job started by alex — job id rb-1775-01. Logs: https://deploys/internal/rb-1775-01

maya (security): good. Next: rotate service tokens that wrote to the archived bucket and revoke any long-lived keys used by logshipper. Suggested immediate actions:
- revoke s3:staging-archiver service-token
- disable pipeline staging-archiver-to-s3
- start KMS key rotation for archive-key-01

alex (oncall-sre): executing revoke on s3 token now. Command:
```
aws iam update-access-key --user staging-archiver --access-key-id AKIA... --status Inactive
```

alex (oncall-sre): disabled pipeline in control plane (staging-archiver-to-s3 -> PAUSED).

maya (security): I'm generating a short list of potentially impacted tokens/keys. Also creating an evidence snapshot and preserving the original archived bucket (make a read-only snapshot) — don't delete objects yet.

emily (product-support): heads up — I already have two customer tickets showing intermittent auth errors starting ~05:02PT. I'll draft an initial customer-facing note saying we're investigating and suspect a logging leak; will update after root cause confirmed.

legal: please coordinate on whether a regulatory notice is needed. Share the list of affected tenants once we have it.

jorge (eng-runtime): quick check: are any production runtime keys in that logstream? My cursory grep on the preserved snapshot found masked keys and a few unmasked bearer fragments for a staging service only. I will run a wider search.

maya (security): if production tokens are found, escalate to legal and CSM immediately. For now treat as staging-priority but proceed with key rotation across staging/prod service accounts that share token manager policies.

alex (oncall-sre): I'm creating a short mitigation playbook in the incident doc and assigning follow-ups. Immediate tasks:
- [alex] block IPs at WAF (done)
- [alex] pause log pipeline (done)
- [alex] revoke s3 service-token (done)
- [maya] rotate KMS key scheduled (in progress)
- [jorge] scan preserved snapshot for unmasked tokens (in progress)
- [emily] customer comms draft (in progress)

maya (security): noticed the debug flag flip was tied to a canary tag 'edge-canary-2026-03-15'. Creating a postmortem task to tighten deploy gating for debug-level flags.

infra-bot: key-rotation jobs queued: kms-rotate-archive-key-01 (job 9921), svcacct-rotate-staging-archiver (job 9922).

alex (oncall-sre): timeline so far: alert 1775022222 -> WAF block + pipeline pause + token revoke by 1775022300. Next 30m: confirm snapshot scan and KMS rotation status. I'll remain in thread until handoff to SRE daytime lead.

maya (security): recommend 1) treat as contained for now, 2) complete rotations and forward evidence to forensics, 3) schedule customer reach-back if any customer tokens are implicated. I'll prepare action items for the incident board.

emily (product-support): posting initial customer note to the shared drive now. Short -> we are investigating auth errors; mitigation in progress; no evidence of customer data breach at this time. Will update in 1h or on major changes. cc @cs-team

alex (oncall-sre): handing off to jorge (day lead) at 1775022405. jorge, please take the incident to post-acute and coordinate with maya + legal + support.

jorge (eng-runtime): ack. I'll take it. I'll post a status update in 20m with scan results. Thanks all.

maya (security): tagging this for post-incident follow-ups: deploy gating for debug flags, log redaction enforcement, automated token-scan on archived buckets, and a runbook for immediate revokes.

legal: standing by for tenant list if any prod tenants are impacted.

pagerbot: incident 1775022222 marked CONTEXT=AUTH-LOG-EXPOSURE. Severity downgraded to P2 after containment at 1775022410.

alex (oncall-sre): closing my oncall handover. If anything spikes re-open the pager. :thumbsup:
